lines.watchItem: TSMC's CoWoS packaging stays sold out into 2027 with waits of 52 to 78 weeks, yet the supply gap is set to narrow from about 20% to 10% by end 2026 as its capacity ramps and outside packagers add lines. Watch whether that easing holds or fresh demand refills the freed capacity.

High-bandwidth memory is tightening into the harder cap on bookable GPU revenue, with HBM4 contract prices set to roughly double into 2027 and each part eating three times the wafer space of standard memory. Watch whether memory, rather than packaging, becomes the limiting input.

Merchant-GPU pull is very strong, with NVIDIA data-center revenue at a record $75.2 billion, up 92% year over year, and AI demand spreading across nodes keeps leading-edge capacity full. Watch whether that pull sustains planned wafer starts.

Custom ASICs are projected to grow 44.6% in 2026 versus 16.1% for merchant GPUs and to pass GPU shipments by 2028, while the top three packaging clients hold over 85% of output with NVIDIA near 60%. Watch how the leading-node customer base tilts between merchant GPUs and hyperscaler custom silicon.

Anthropic is in early talks with Samsung to build a custom AI chip on a 2nm process, one sign hyperscalers are spreading leading-node work beyond merchant GPUs. Watch whether such second-source moves pull custom-silicon volume toward other foundries.

TSMC posted a 67.7% gross margin, up 9.1 points year over year, and AI demand broadening across nodes and packaging is handing foundries pricing power, with HBM prices set to double. Watch whether firm end-market pricing keeps that pricing power across the chain.

Taiwanese prosecutors have escalated a smuggling probe into Nvidia AI chips routed to China, raiding Supermicro sites over roughly $2.5 billion of servers as export enforcement intensifies. Watch how tighter controls bear on addressable merchant-GPU demand.
